rules.currentBehavior: V17 validates audio warp maps on both timeline and Project Bin audio clips. A map has 2 through 4,096 closed points with canonical reduced rational outer and source positions, strictly increasing outer and source domains, and forward mode only. Its outer endpoints match the resolved clip anchor extent and its source endpoints match the clip source extent. Sample-anchored maps use sample frames; musical maps require a beat extent and exact tempo authority; reversed clips reject. A valid Project Bin map survives project-bin/place as a distinct timeline clip ID with null binItemId and the same exact map, then passes V17 validation. Nonempty state reconciles exactly one reserved soundscaper.audio-warp requirement for org.soundscaper.capability.audio-warp with display name Audio warp maps, disposition bypass, and fallback null; empty state invents no requirement. Authored state refuses publisher substitution. audioWarp is true in Soundscaper and in the production capability register, so compatibility is available/native, compatible, and writable. It is false but registered in Framescaper, so compatibility is unavailable/bypassed and incompatible and activation is intrinsically read-only. The capability is excluded from both audio and video rendered-fallback eligibility sets; publisher-authored substitution or rendered fallback rejects. Transient identity binds the canonical full-source PCM SHA-256 digest, exact source range, channel policy, normalized analysis parameters, and algorithm revision. A missing digest is resolved by streaming the full canonical source under storage-generation checks; exact range reading is bounded before allocation and opens only intersecting generation-bound chunks. Transient records persist only in the disposable derived analysis cache, never project JSON. Each record binds its key and payload SHA-256 and contains a bounded transient array; corrupt or stale records are discarded. Aggregate count, useful-byte, and age LRU retention is enforced separately by the cache repository. Because no authoritative digest-to-source index exists, successful source deletion and retention pruning conservatively purge the whole transient payload and companion namespaces. Cache state never roots pruning, unrelated analysis survives, and a disposable cleanup fault cannot roll back or reject authoritative source deletion. That cache lifecycle is not a bound on the project document, and V17 has no transient-analysis array. Exact map algebra and its evaluator drive playback, waveform projection, trim, split, exact offline fallback, and export. The runtime never substitutes scalar output-length conversion: realtime segments derive exact source-position endpoints and a piecewise linear projection from the same map. A maintained nonidentity production-path browser fixture proves PCM parity within the 0.000001 signal-error budget in Chromium and Firefox. When realtime acceleration is absent, the bounded exact fallback admits only the effect-free stateless dry, gain, pan, mute, envelope, and fade path; every enabled processor in an included track, bus, send, or master rack rejects before render. Playback retains the current window and exactly one window ahead; a missed deadline stops playback and never time-shifts the next window, so gapless playback is not guaranteed. Soundscaper exposes the workflow only through the Effect > Pitch and tempo menu for a selected unlocked audio clip, with analyze, identity-map, add, move, delete, quantize, groove, and clear actions. Browser evidence exercises keyboard operation, screen-reader names and roles, serious axe checks, and forced colors. Framescaper exposes no audio-warp menu or surface.

Enabled maintained effects on timeline and Project Bin video clips become minimal disabled activation copies; disabled effects and missing, foreign, or wrong-kind stacks remain untouched. Stable clip and effect IDs are bounded to 256 characters, effect types to 128 characters, the lower-only production ceiling is 4,096 affected effects across both locations, and overflow rejects instead of truncating. Each placeholder entry records only location, clip ID, effect ID, and effect type without reading or retaining params, context, state, or other opaque payloads. Only transient engine loading receives the project projection, and the WebGL preview filters exact affected effects from timeline stacks using trusted metadata while caching selectors and preserving unchanged stack references. The canonical project, history, source loading, persistence, save, and export or offline-render paths remain unchanged. Projection metadata is deeply frozen across per-tab session clones and the document snapshot. The active compatibility notice matches that metadata to one qualifying requirement and renders localized control-free affected-effect placeholders with maintained effect labels and canonical Timeline or Project Bin clip ownership without reading effect payloads. Future schemas return unchanged before clip or Project Bin traversal. This rule does not cover unknown or third-party effects, rendered-fallback substitution, export or offline render behavior, per-feature activation controls, arbitrary future schemas, or earlier Soundscaper project schemas.

rules.requiredOutcome: On maintained exact-current-schema activation, exactly one requirement declared for rendered fallback may replace canonical video paths for editor playback through one of two closed relationships. The project-video-render-v1 role accepts an unavailable or unknown canonical namespaced feature identity and uses an admitted full-source render; the unavailable-only video-clip-render-v1 role remains restricted to exact videoEffects and may replace one exact target clip with its complete admitted render. The same exact fallback may reach maintained video export only when role- and target-bound operation-time admission under the export signal returns the exact canonical native Blob it size-checks and hashes for direct immutable-byte reuse, while the canonical project remains intrinsically read-only and unmodified and playback activation stays visibly identified. Final-video delivery may additionally compose one qualifying audio whole-mix fallback with one maintained video fallback through joint operation-time admission that returns the private chunk provider and exact verified Blob. Portable .scape and explicit managed desktop handoff to a fresh recipient must preserve the clip relationship and manifest-only fallback body, with the controller separately verifying the manifest fallback digest before activation and again for later delivery.
rules.currentBehavior: The controller evaluates the authoritative actual project history and projects only exact schema 17 when its soundscaper-project report contains exactly one qualifying item. The project-video-render-v1 role accepts a canonical namespaced feature ID reported unavailable or unknown; the video-clip-render-v1 role accepts only exact videoEffects reported unavailable. Both require declared and effective rendered-fallback dispositions, and the report's video descriptor must exactly match the canonical manifest requirement by requirement ID, feature ID, disposition, role, optional target clip ID, video kind, source ID, and SHA-256. The existing project-fallback-integrity admission separately verifies the actual local body against that digest before activation side effects. For final-video delivery it derives an exact video selector from the active video fallback's requirement ID, feature ID, role, target clip ID, video kind, source ID, and SHA-256 and may pair it with the exact active audio selector of either closed audio role under the export task signal. One joint selector-mode verification receives the active audio and video selectors, applies their cumulative non-raiseable 64 GiB preflight before both selected body reads, performs a full canonical audio chunk scan first to return its digest-bound private chunk provider, then size-checks and hashes the selected video body's canonical native Blob and retains that exact immutable Blob before video planning, storage preflight, audio rendering, FFmpeg, or output publication. Nonselected fallback bodies are not read. Export retrieves it only with the exact selector and directly reuses the same Blob without a second fallback storage read. For project-video-render-v1, the referenced source must have the exact video kind, match the project sample rate, and carry a positive safe-integer frame count, width, and height plus a positive finite frame rate. Missing or duplicated sources, multiple qualifying candidates, descriptor drift, invalid geometry, and reserved synthetic track or clip ID collisions across the timeline or Project Bin reject. Its transient projection replaces all timeline video clips and tracks with one neutral clip and track using the full source from frame zero while preserving audio and label clips and tracks, the exact Project Bin and sources, and every other canonical field. The video-clip-render-v1 role is restricted to videoEffects and one exact target clip ID with an enabled maintained video effect. Its video fallback source must be different from the canonical source, declare hasAudio false, have frame count equal to the target duration, and match the sample rate, width, height, and frame rate of that canonical source. Its transient projection replaces only the target timeline clip's source with the complete render: source starts at frame zero, trims become zero, speed becomes one, and video effects become empty. Track membership, timeline placement, duration, group, A/V link, layer and transition context, every unaffected clip and source, and the canonical project and history stay unchanged. Ordinary video composition and export consume that projected target alongside normally loaded unaffected video. A manifest-only fallback becomes an explicit required video source and is activated before the transient project reaches the engine or preview. The document snapshot supplies that transient preview project, and the WebGL preview resolves each projected clip through the exact projected source identity after exact clip lookup. Deeply frozen per-tab and document-snapshot metadata and the localized source/component UI bind the exact feature ID and requirement ID without exposing the source ID or digest. The maintained video delivery projection applies the active audio rendered-fallback projection of either closed audio role first and then the selected video rendered fallback. It represents at most one audio and one video fallback and reapplies exactly the audio and video effect bypasses playback applied, so a bypassed effect never reappears in the delivered file; unrepresented, duplicate same-kind, unsupported-role, or additional rendered fallbacks reject instead of exporting a partial projection. The exact admitted Blob is the full-project plan's only video input or the clip-local plan's selected target input; canonical and unaffected clip-local video inputs continue through ordinary loading. An active audio whole-mix renders through an empty private buffer map and its sole exact chunk source without committed time/pitch cache preparation; an active audio track render instead keeps ordinary lane buffers and providers beside its private fallback provider, which replaces any ordinary representation of the fallback source, with committed time/pitch caches prepared for the native lanes; otherwise canonical audio clips and effects remain in the delivery snapshot and render into the separate staged audio mix. Embedded fallback-video audio is neither extracted nor mapped. The canonical project, history, persistence, and save state remain read-only and unmodified. Export asserts project, task, and generation currentness before verification and after verification, binds the integrity admission to the canonical project and exact selector, reasserts currentness after FFmpeg before output handling, passes the owned signal to output publication, and rechecks currentness after publication with cleanup for a recoverable stale result; verification refusal or cancellation starts no plan, storage preflight, audio render, FFmpeg call, or output publication. The org.example.future-video-pipeline unknown-feature composed headless Framescaper-to-fresh-Soundscaper exact schema 17 fixture proves explicit managed whole-Blob handoff of an editable retained original and a manifest-only whole-project fallback. A separate video-clip-render-v1 managed handoff fixture carries the canonical target, unaffected video, and manifest-only fallback into a fresh recipient. The recipient preserves the exact target clip ID and fallback body digest in its canonical shadow and reopens it before relationship-bound integrity admission and playback. Managed transfer authenticates each descriptor and body digest, not the manifest declaration. Portable .scape likewise round-trips the relationship; copy collision remaps the fallback source ID while preserving the target clip ID. Corrupting a fallback after activation proves that operation-time verification rejects delivery before FFmpeg and output; restoring the exact body produces delivery that reuses the newly verified Blob while the canonical document remains unchanged. The exact one-audio/one-video final-video composition is qualified. More than one qualifying video fallback across canonical feature identities rejects as ambiguous; multiple clip fallbacks, duplicate same-kind fallbacks, and other mixed fallback relationships are unqualified. Audio-kind descriptors of either closed audio role never qualify as the video relationship; the delivery layer admits only the separate exact audio roles, and noncanonical feature IDs fail manifest admission. Unknown canonical feature identities qualify only for project-video-render-v1 and do not authorize third-party feature-code activation. Future schemas and earlier Soundscaper schemas remain outside this rule. Linked-only or unmanaged delivery and simultaneous rendered fallback delivery beyond that exact composition are unqualified; for standalone audio delivery, simultaneous rendered fallbacks still reject. Generic fallback authoring and other relationship roles are unqualified, as are freeze, unfreeze, proxy or relink relationships, embedded fallback-video audio, every nonselected fallback-body claim, and other export or offline-render parity. Source/component UI binding is qualified, and the exact Linux x64 packaged workflow qualifies activation and transport playback for both frozen video roles. Packaged runtime or UI final-delivery workflows are unqualified, browser behavior and codec qualification are unqualified, and range transport and reference-scale evidence are unqualified. The operation provides no durable storage-record or byte lease, guarantee against cross-process replacement after admission, or whole-handoff atomicity.

rules.requiredOutcome: Every rendered fallback referenced by an exact-current-schema raw or stored project admitted through the maintained controller is verified against its canonical local stored bytes before activation side effects. Maintained exact-schema project-video-render-v1 and videoEffects-only video-clip-render-v1 delivery must independently select its exact active claim at operation time under the export signal, size-check and hash only that canonical native video Blob, and directly reuse the admitted immutable bytes; final-video delivery may additionally pair that exact video claim with one role-defined audio whole-mix claim so that a single joint operation-time admission returns both the digest-bound private chunk provider and that exact Blob before video planning, other media work, FFmpeg, or output publication. Standalone final-mix audio delivery must still refuse simultaneous rendered fallbacks.
rules.currentBehavior: The controller verifies the authoritative exact-schema-17 activation project, including existing same-ID tab history bound by a session-owned history token. After verification it obtains one exclusive session activation reservation before project-generation invalidation, recording or engine shutdown, lock changes, ordinary engine-source loading, or normal activation persistence. The reservation rejects target history replacement, close/reopen, and competing active-project publication through synchronous session publication and is released in finally. Admission reads publish no storage maintenance. Audio claims hash the canonical audio-f32le-chunks-v1 sequence through the same checked PCM geometry and cumulative 65,536-chunk ceiling as .scape export. Video claims hash a genuine immutable original-media Blob body incrementally through the non-raiseable 4 MiB media-digest window. Unique claimed audio bytes and admitted video sizes share a non-raiseable 64 GiB cumulative ceiling before fallback body reads. Verification is sequential and cooperatively cancellable through the maintained store. Read-only video-metadata preflight is raced against cancellation, so an injected signal-ignoring provider may continue after admission rejects; a provider-stalled fallback body read can instead delay cancellation settlement and iterator cleanup. Verification deduplicates identical source claims and rejects conflicting digests or conflicting relationship roles and target clip or track IDs before storage reads. It rejects missing, malformed, or mismatched local assets. Empty manifests and future schemas perform no asset reads, and future featureRequirements are not traversed. The maintained final-video delivery path invokes this verifier afresh against the canonical project under the owned export task signal through one joint verification call whose singular selector options describe the active audio and video claims by the active requirement ID, feature ID, relationship role, the video relationship's target clip ID or the audio track relationship's target track ID, media kind, source ID, and SHA-256. The audio selector's role is the closed project-audio-mix-v1 or audio-track-render-v1 union: the whole-mix role binds a null target and the track role binds one exact target track ID. The admission snapshot binds that role and target ID together with the target clip's canonical source, duration, maintained video effects, the target track's type, rack activity, effect identity and inertness flags, lane membership, and exact lane placement, and the source geometry needed by the relationship; role, target, or context drift fails currentness, and a lane or rack change that breaks the declared geometry fails admission capture itself, which the currentness fence reports as an admission change. That joint call applies one cumulative non-raiseable 64 GiB expanded-byte ceiling across the selected targets, charging the audio target first, before their fallback body reads; it then scans the selected audio source's full canonical audio-f32le-chunks-v1 sequence first and returns a digest-bound private chunk provider, and only then loads, size-checks, and hashes the selected canonical native video Blob and retains that exact immutable Blob. Nonselected fallback bodies are not read, and each admitted representation is released only for its own exact selector. Every provider read reruns the caller fence together with the full admission-state recheck of every verified selector, so in the composed case drift in the selected video requirement aborts an audio provider read. Export asserts task, project-generation, and operation currentness before verification, asserts the returned admission against that canonical project and each exact selector, and repeats the operation fences after verification before any plan, storage preflight, audio render, FFmpeg call, or output publication. Delivery directly reuses the admitted Blob as the whole-project plan's sole video input or the clip-local plan's selected target input without a second fallback storage read, checks currentness again after FFmpeg, passes the owned signal to publication, and rechecks currentness after publication with cleanup for a recoverable stale result. A mismatch or cancellation reaches no later delivery work. The joint call is sequential and not transactional; a cancellation after the audio scan leaves that body already read and retains no partial admission. The standalone final-mix audio delivery path invokes the same verifier with only its audio selector and still rejects simultaneous rendered fallbacks of any kind. Admission is point-in-time: the retained audio chunk provider proves only that a chunk is unchanged since this admission, and video delivery is immutable-Blob identity reuse of a Blob hashed once during it and not rehashed on retrieval, not a durable lease over the managed storage record or a guarantee against later low-level or cross-process replacement of that storage binding. This rule does not verify a nonselected fallback body, authorize simultaneous rendered-fallback delivery beyond the exact one-audio/one-video final-video composition, cover arbitrary direct store.loadProject calls, establish publisher authenticity, authorize other-role, third-party feature-code, linked-only, or unmanaged fallback delivery, substitute fallback media by itself, or provide a complete third-party activation gate.

rules.requiredOutcome: Current-format portable archive inspection evaluates maintained project feature requirements against the selected product before collision lookup, import, persistence, or activation without interpreting future project schemas.
rules.currentBehavior: The selected product is snapshotted through the shared compatibility service and injected into inspection as a provider-owned option after caller options, so a caller cannot override it. After current-format archive integrity, project-source validation, and rendered-fallback claim-to-descriptor binding, exact schema 17 is evaluated before project collision lookup and returned as a deeply frozen featureRequirementsCompatibility report. Inspection does not hash asset bodies. Future project schemas return null and featureRequirements is not traversed. This programmatic surface is the foundation for the maintained open decision; it does not use fallbacks at runtime or gate third-party activation.

rules.requiredOutcome: Every current-format, exact-current-schema archive opened through the maintained workspace/UI file routes with an incompatible selected-product feature report requires explicit compatibility-bearing consent or cancellation before import, persistence, or activation, in both collision and no-collision flows.
rules.currentBehavior: Maintained workspace/UI file-open routes use one replaceable owned request from inspection through a closed decision. A no-collision incompatible report permits only open-read-only or cancel; a combined incompatibility and ID collision permits only copy-read-only or cancel in one decision; compatible collisions permit only copy or cancel. Distinct compatibility-bearing choices fail closed against stale collision callbacks. Cancel resolves before native import, persistence, or activation. The localized dialog exposes bounded display names, stable feature IDs, availability, and declared disposition without claiming fallback verification or runtime use; incompatible decisions default focus to Cancel and support Escape dismissal and focus restoration. Acceptance passes only the existing copy collision policy into native open, after which the controller reevaluates the actual project history and enforces it as intrinsically read-only. Future-schema null reports skip this decision. The low-level native-open API retains its caller-supplied collision policy, and it and third-party activation remain outside this rule.

rules.requiredOutcome: A raw project document with a newer schema is cloned without normalization and cannot enter a mutation or overwrite path.
rules.currentBehavior: The core migration boundary returns newer objects as structured clones with readOnly=true and reason=newer-schema.

rules.requiredOutcome: A future-schema portable archive opens read-only and can be exported unchanged without ID, storage-key, binary, or unknown-field loss.
rules.currentBehavior: A format-1 archive whose project document carries a schema greater than 12 opens read-only without graph interpretation: the importer returns the unmutated document before collision or source-identity rewriting, asset extraction, or store publication, and the native service retains the original archive so save-copy publishes an exact byte copy. The unchanged-copy publisher validates only the envelope, the digest-bound project document, and the future schema-version scalar, refuses current-schema, mismatched, tampered, and unknown-format archives before any bytes flow, and never repacks, so IDs, storage keys, binary state, and unknown entries survive byte-identically. Editing remains refused and unknown archive format versions remain rejected before persistence.

rules.requiredOutcome: Designated JSON opaque extension fields survive clone, save, and portable archive reopen semantically unchanged.
rules.currentBehavior: JSON-compatible opaqueExtensions survive exact-current-schema clone and .scape round trips; older pre-release raw schemas require source-media re-import and are not normalized.

rules.requiredOutcome: Supported Uint8Array and ArrayBuffer opaque state in exact-current-schema, current-format .scape projects uses a tagged, bounded JSON encoding and round-trips byte-exactly without activation.
rules.currentBehavior: Before JSON.parse, every schema receives an iterative raw-JSON structural preflight bounded to 101,536 values and depth 130 in production; the descriptor allowance preserves round-trip closure for the bounded tagged representation. Exact schema 17 export encodes Uint8Array values, offset-view bytes, and ArrayBuffer values with a reserved tagged descriptor; export and post-parse decode independently enforce the lower-only logical limits of 100,000 traversal nodes and depth 128, while other ArrayBuffer views reject. The binary budget also admits at most 256 payloads, 4 MiB per payload, and 8 MiB aggregate bytes. Import and inspection validate the closed descriptor schema, unique positive IDs, canonical base64, exact byte lengths, and all limits before allocating decoded payloads, then restore the declared binary type without interpreting its bytes. Reserved-tag collisions, project-container accessors, and callable container toJSON hooks reject without invocation. Future-schema tag-shaped data is structurally counted by the raw preflight but is neither decoded nor interpreted as a binary descriptor.

rules.requiredOutcome: Unavailable native features remain visible and bypassable, retain editable opaque state, declare requirements, and reference an audible or visible fallback when available.
rules.currentBehavior: The schema 17 manifest, evaluator, retention roots, current-format .scape paths, selected-product controller report, and current-format .scape inspection report preserve and classify declared requirements. Maintained exact-schema-17 create, load, clone, and commit paths reconcile the owned first-party audio- and video-effects requirements. The bounded first-party audio-effect slice loads qualifying unavailable rack processors through a transient engine bypass projection, and the bounded first-party video-effect slice loads minimal disabled activation copies and filters exact affected effects from timeline stacks in WebGL preview; persistent localized control-free affected-object placeholders follow the active tab for both slices. Separate exact-schema-17 role-defined audio whole-mix, first-party audioEffects-only track-local audio, and whole-project video or first-party videoEffects-only clip-local fallback slices substitute admitted sources for editor playback while canonical state remains read-only and unchanged and the active tab identifies fallback use. The video whole-project role replaces timeline video with a neutral full-source clip at frame zero; the closed clip role replaces only its exact target after separate controller body and relationship verification and required-source activation. Maintained video export uses the corresponding projection after selector-bound operation-time admission returns the exact size- and digest-verified canonical native Blob without a second storage read; the full-project Blob is the sole video input, while the clip-local Blob is one selected target input beside unaffected ordinary video. Selector mode does not read a nonselected fallback body. Final-video delivery may additionally compose that video fallback with one role-defined audio fallback of either closed audio role through a single joint operation-time admission, and that exact one-audio/one-video final-video composition is qualified; an active whole-mix renders through its private chunk source as the sole audio input, an active track render keeps ordinary lane sources beside that private provider, and otherwise canonical audio remains a separately staged mix, and embedded fallback-video audio is not used. Maintained opens provide an actionable pre-open read-only or cancel decision, the broader persistent document-level post-open report follows the active tab, and the controller still makes an activated project with an unavailable or unknown requirement intrinsically read-only. A separate strictly read-only affected-object index names the canonical objects behind that post-open report: it runs for every maintained feature schema carrying an incompatible soundscaper-project report, reads the live canonical current project rather than the playback projection so later edits stay reflected, is recomputed per document snapshot instead of being retained in tab metadata, and returns one deeply frozen entry per unavailable or unknown item of that retained activation-time report and nothing when there is none. The pass is total on that snapshot path: only a ceiling option that is not a non-negative safe integer at or below the production limit throws, an accessor in a named-property position is treated as absent rather than invoked or thrown on, and a missing, empty, or over-long stable ID or object type skips that object instead of rejecting, because schema 17 bounds no such string length and a throw during snapshot construction would blank the editor; array elements are still read by ordinary indexed access, so that accessor guarantee covers named property reads only and not array membership. Attribution follows the declared fallback descriptor rather than the outcome of playback qualification or integrity admission, so a video-clip-render-v1 descriptor reported unknown is still indexed and labelled as replaced during editor playback even though that role qualifies for playback only when its availability is unavailable. A carried fallback attributes the canonical objects its declared role replaces: project-audio-mix-v1 names every non-label, non-video track rack, mixer group, mixer send, and master rack together with every non-video timeline clip; project-video-render-v1 names the video tracks as well as the timeline video clips its projection collapses; audio-track-render-v1 names the declared target track together with each timeline clip its lane anchors; and any other role names only the timeline clip whose ID matches the declared target. A requirement carrying no fallback descriptor is attributed only when its feature ID is the owned audioEffects or videoEffects capability, and those two channels collect only effects whose type is outside the maintained registry, because a registered type already has its own first-party placeholder section and collecting it would spend the shared ceiling on rows the notice discards; they also honour the inertness gates the sibling bypass applies, the audio channel skipping an inactive rack and a disabled or already-bypassed effect across those same racks and the video channel skipping a disabled effect across timeline and Project Bin video clips. Their reach is asymmetric: open normalization rejects a foreign video-effect type outright, so the video-effect channel is reachable in principle but not by any project that opens, and an unregistered type is an audio-rack phenomenon in practice. A channel that names no object at all, whether a requirement outside those channels, a declared target clip absent from the current project, or a video role in a project holding no video object, leaves the requirement unattributable with an empty list, and the notice then states explicitly that its affected objects cannot be identified rather than rendering nothing. The index reads only the project schema version, object IDs, types, clip kinds, and the active, enabled, and bypassed flags it gates on, never effect params, context, state, or opaque payloads, and it projects, mutates, and bypasses nothing while reading that canonical state. Its lower-only 4,096-object ceiling is shared across the whole index and bounds the retained list rather than the traversal: enumeration continues after the ceiling is exhausted, the index is recomputed for every snapshot of any incompatible maintained document, and it truncates and discloses a per-requirement omitted-object count where the sibling bypass slices reject instead, because dropping an entry from a read-only list cannot leave an unavailable effect audible; an owner track, rack, or clip whose own ID cannot be read is skipped silently and is not counted in that disclosure. It adds no bypass, activation, read-only-enforcement, engine, export, or delivery behavior, makes no listed object controllable, and grants no capability to an unknown or third-party feature. Current-format exact-schema .scape archive fallback integrity verifies the declared digest and relationship against the canonical asset, while inspection performs pre-collision descriptor binding without reading asset bodies. Maintained exact-schema-17 controller activation verifies referenced local audio and video fallback bytes before activation side effects, and the maintained video delivery path independently verifies the selected active video claim, together with any paired active audio claim of either closed audio role, before planning or other media work and reuses the admitted immutable Blob. The bounded current-schema .scape codec preserves supported Uint8Array and ArrayBuffer opaque native/effect state byte-exactly without activation; other buffer views remain unsupported. Per-feature bypass controls beyond these maintained first-party slices, generic per-object placeholders for a requirement outside those closed attribution channels, rendered-fallback runtime use beyond the closed audio whole-mix, audio track, and maintained video relationships, simultaneous fallback delivery beyond that composition, fallback-authoring workflows beyond the closed relationship, and arbitrary future-schema archive preservation are not implemented.

rules.requiredOutcome: Video originals and reproducible proxies retain an explicit relationship, and proxy use never changes editorial time or original delivery semantics.
rules.currentBehavior: Video source originals remain authoritative for editorial time, extracted audio, relink identity, browser and native rendering, export, and delivery. Framescaper generates a proxy from an original with the shipped FFmpeg under one maintained recipe that keeps every frame at the presentation time the original gave it, writes display geometry with square pixels, and carries no audio; the observer digests and probes the result, and exact timing conformance refuses a body whose boundaries drift. The selected F31 lazy menu workflow delegates through its immutable V28 foundation and supports generation, attach existing, detach, relink, regenerate, and Original, Proxy, or Auto preview selection with bounded progress and cancellation. Candidate publication proves the body before an atomic stale-safe history swap, leaves the tab editable, and cleans partial or superseded claims without exposing them. Ordinary edits carry an attachment forward only while the source digest, conformed frame count, and occurrence ownership remain true; changed-content relink, replace, reprobe, reimport, trim-media, consolidate, or removing the last occurrence drops stale state in the same transaction, while an identical original relink preserves and reattests it. Preview reattests each session through bounded body hashing, timing validation, an ephemeral bound view, and current-original conformance before showing proxy pictures. Original, Proxy, and Auto selection occurs in the source domain before occurrence retime, so retiming does not detach a conformant attachment or make it timing authority. Auto adapts from reported preview pressure, and a valid proxy can preserve editing and preview while the original is offline. Browser export, the selected V14 evaluated-RGBA carrier, and final delivery always authenticate and select the original and visibly refuse while it is unavailable. Framescaper owns the videoProxy requirement, while Soundscaper receives V18 attachments only as copy-only preservation. Exact-schema-17 rendered-fallback relationships remain separate and are not original-to-proxy relationships.

rules.requiredOutcome: Freeze, unfreeze, commit, and rendered fallback state preserve the editable source and native-effect metadata.
rules.currentBehavior: Selected Soundscaper V23 owns audio-track freeze, refresh, unfreeze, and commit through exact expected-state commands and one history transaction. Freeze captures post-insert, pre-strip audio while retaining editable clips, the insert rack, strip automation, and routing; no PCM enters project JSON. Freshness is digest-bound to the exact clip and verified source-content identities, rack state, effect automation, render interval, and sample rate. Only a fresh record owns an audio-track-render-v1 rendered fallback bound to its verified derived-source SHA-256; a stale or unverifiable record remains editable but reconciles to bypass with no fallback and is never selected for playback. Browser storage, format-1 Scape, managed handoff, and the product-owned Soundscaper desktop V10 library preserve the relationship and verify its PCM body before activation. Administrative Scape source-ID remapping rebinds only a previously admitted fresh relationship, while stale state retains its old digest authority. Framescaper keeps audioTrackFreeze unavailable and can only custody an exact V23 archive opaquely for byte-stable return.
